About the company

Hi, we're Ondo Finance. Our mission is to provide institutional-grade, blockchain-enabled investment products and services. We have both a technology arm that develops decentralized finance technology, and an asset management arm that creates and manages tokenized funds. We were the first company to tokenize exposure to US Treasuries, and have since expanded into several other assets. We are also focused on incubating protocols that can support both tokenized real-world assets and traditional crypto.

Founded by folks from Goldman Sachs Digital Assets Team, we’re backed by some of the best investors in the world including Founders Fund, Coinbase Ventures, Pantera Capital, Tiger Global, and more. We are currently the leaders in the space in terms of AUM and are well capitalized to continue growing the firm. We're fully remote, with team members across the U.S.

About the Role

We’re looking for a highly organized, proactive, and execution-driven Senior Event Manager (Contract-to-Full-Time) to join Ondo Finance. This position will initially begin as a full-time contract role, with the opportunity to transition into a permanent full-time position based on performance, business needs, and mutual fit. This role will partner closely with the Marketing Events Lead to support the delivery of Ondo’s global event strategy.

Reporting to the Marketing Events Lead, this role will play a key part in executing Ondo’s global event strategy, managing internal offsites and supporting high-impact external events, including industry conferences, partner activations, executive gatherings, and institutional events.

You’ll be responsible for managing multiple event workstreams from planning through execution, ensuring timelines, budgets, vendors, and deliverables are organized and on track. We're looking for someone who can operate independently, anticipate needs, proactively communicate updates, and take full ownership of assigned projects.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, global environment, has exceptional attention to detail, and enjoys building scalable processes that improve how events are planned and executed.

Target outcomes 

  • Seamless delivery of internal offsites and external event activations, with high stakeholder satisfaction
  • Successful execution of Ondo’s global event strategy through reliable operational ownership and support
  • Consistent delivery of multiple concurrent event workstreams on time and within budget
  • Strong stakeholder confidence through proactive communication, accountability, and timely follow-through
  • High-quality attendee, speaker, and partner experiences across events
  • Scalable event operations supported by efficient processes, documentation, and technology

Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end planning and execution of internal offsites including leadership, team, and company-wide, ensuring high-quality delivery
  • Manage assigned external event workstreams, including industry conferences, sponsorships, partner activations, VIP receptions, and institutional gatherings
  • Source venues, negotiate contracts, and manage relationships with hotels, production agencies, AV providers, caterers, and other vendors
  • Develop and maintain event timelines, project trackers, budgets, production schedules, run of show, and logistics documentation
  • Manage multiple concurrent projects, ensuring deadlines, deliverables, and stakeholder expectations are met
  • Proactively communicate project updates, identify potential risks or blockers, and recommend solutions before issues escalate
  • Oversee attendee registration, communications, travel coordination, accommodations, and overall guest experience
  • Manage event budgets, invoices, payment coordination, and post-event financial reconciliation
  • Coordinate speaker logistics, including onboarding, scheduling, travel, presentations, and onsite management
  • Manage sponsorship deliverables, branding requirements, and partner commitments
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Marketing, Design, GTM, Leadership, Legal, Finance, and other internal teams
  • Coordinate with external agencies and production partners to ensure seamless event execution
  • Maintain accurate, centralized event documentation, trackers, vendor information, and post-event reporting
  • Lead post-event evaluations, including stakeholder feedback, key learnings, and recommendations to improve future events
  • Develop and refine event playbooks, templates, workflows, and operational processes to support a growing global events program
  • Identify opportunities to leverage technology, automation, and AI to streamline event planning, coordination, and reporting
  • Support onsite execution for domestic and international events as needed

Requirements

  • 8+ years of experience in event management, production, or operations, with demonstrated ownership of complex corporate events
  • Proven experience independently managing events from initial planning through onsite execution
  • Strong background in venue sourcing, contract negotiation, vendor management, budgeting, and event production
  • Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously
  • Strong problem-solving skills and sound judgment, with the ability to make informed decisions independently and know when to escalate issues
  • Demonstrated ability to take initiative, anticipate challenges, and proactively resolve issues with minimal oversight
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide clear, timely updates and effectively manage stakeholder expectations
  • Proven track record of meeting deadlines, following through on commitments, and maintaining accurate project documentation
  • Experience collaborating with senior leadership and cross-functional teams
  • Comfortable operating in a fast-paced, evolving environment with shifting priorities
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and event/project management tools
  • Interest in leveraging AI, automation, and technology to improve operational efficiency
  • Willingness to travel domestically and internationally to support onsite event execution
  • Based in PT, MT, CT, ET or APAC time zones

Nice to haves 

  • Experience producing executive-level, institutional, or high-touch VIP events
  • Experience in TradFi, fintech, crypto, or DeFi
  • Experience managing global events across North America, EMEA, APAC, and LATAM
  • Experience working with external production agencies and managing complex vendor relationships
  • Familiarity with event registration platforms, CRM systems, and event marketing tools

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation including but not limited to salary, future token rights, and/or equity (according to your preferences) — We are well-funded and believe that great talent deserves great compensation.
  • Full benefits (medical, vision, and dental) and flexible vacation policy (PTO).
  • Remote-first team across many countries — You will be an early team member helping shape our vision, culture, and design practices.
  • A+ colleagues — Our team includes alumni from: Goldman Sachs, Blackrock, Two Sigma, Bridgewater, SpaceX, AWS, Meta, Google, McKinsey, Circle, Uniswap.
  • Best-in-class investors — We are proud to be backed by leading crypto experts and VCs, including Pantera Capital, Founders Fund and Coinbase Ventures.
descriptions.job-0nth22p:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We’re a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position 
Work from anywhere!

Position overview

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

The mandate

  1. Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional.
    You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
  2. Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would.
    You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
  3. Win the right members, efficiently.
    You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
  4. Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances.
    Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
  5. Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless.
    You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
  6. Build one Customer organisation, not four.
    Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
  7. Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call.
    You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate

This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

  • You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
  • You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
  • You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
  • You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
  • You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done 

  • 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).
  • Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.
  • Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
  • Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
  • Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
  • Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
  • A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.
Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.
Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

  • Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
  • Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
  • Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
  • Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balance
    Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge. 

  • Expect Excellence
    Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you’ll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Radar helps businesses prevent payments fraud and abuse while enabling legitimate customers to transact with confidence. We combine machine learning and AI with the intelligence of Stripe’s global network to make sophisticated fraud prevention accessible to businesses of all sizes.

Our work spans payments fraud detection, protection against abuse beyond the payment, enterprise APIs that bring Radar’s capabilities into businesses’ own systems and payment flows, and the platform that powers it all. We build everything from reliable, low-latency infrastructure to intuitive tools that help users understand threats and control how they respond.

Fraud evolves constantly, and so do we. We work directly with users to understand emerging attacks, turn advances in ML and AI into effective defenses, and build products that protect and grow their revenue.

What you’ll do

As a software engineer on Radar, you’ll build products and infrastructure that help businesses understand and stop fraud and abuse. Your work will span backend services, enterprise APIs, and user experiences that put sophisticated prevention capabilities into our customers’ hands.

You’ll own problems from investigation through launch, partnering with  product managers, designers, and data scientists. You’ll have opportunities to scale systems that make real-time decisions across Stripe’s global payments network, bring advances in ML and AI into production, and build new products from scratch. Every improvement can have a direct impact on the revenue our users retain and the legitimate customers they serve.

Responsibilities

  • Build and operate reliable, low-latency services that detect and prevent fraud and abuse at scale
  • Design APIs and dashboard experiences that help businesses investigate threats, configure defenses, and understand how Radar protects them
  • Develop the shared platform and infrastructure that enable teams to build and launch new Radar capabilities
  • Work directly with users to understand emerging threats and turn those insights into broadly useful products
  • Partner with ML engineers and data scientists to bring new signals, models, and AI capabilities into production
  • Own projects end to end, from technical design and implementation through rollout, measurement, and iteration
  • Uphold a high bar for engineering quality, reliability, and product craft while moving quickly as threats evolve

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 2+ years of industry software engineering experience
  • Strong coding skills in any programming language, with experience building and maintaining production software
  • Ability to work across systems and technologies, learn unfamiliar codebases, and make thoughtful technical trade-offs
  • A rigorous approach to problem solving, including using data to investigate issues and evaluate whether a solution works
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work across disciplines and contribute to your peers’ success
  • An ownership mindset and comfort navigating ambiguity, taking initiative, and following through on user problems

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building distributed systems or real-time services with demanding reliability and latency requirements
  • Experience building APIs, developer platforms, or intuitive user interfaces for complex workflows
  • Experience bringing ML or AI capabilities into production software
  • Experience working on fraud prevention, abuse prevention, risk, or security
  • Experience taking a product from an early idea to launch and iterating directly with customers

descriptions.job-1yeivpd:
Join us in building the future of finance.

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. We're looking for an exceptional Futures Risk Program Manager to help shape the future of our core platforms, products, and customer experiences. FinTech is one of the most complex and rapidly evolving spaces in technology, and the challenges we're tackling require deep innovation, critical thinking, and scale that don't always have strong precedents. You'll take on a highly influential role shaping vision and execution across key strategic initiatives. You'll partner with cross-functional leaders, contribute to high-impact decisions, guide complex projects from concept to completion, and mentor others on the team. This is a role for someone who leverages modern tools and cutting-edge methodologies as a core part of how they solve problems, and raises the bar for everyone around them.

This role is based in our Chicago, IL, with in-person attendance expected at least five days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you'll do

Design and implement a comprehensive risk management strategy emphasizing early risk detection, automated alert systems, incident response, and continuous improvement. Conduct thorough risk assessments focused on operational and technology risks, identifying vulnerabilities, and recommending mitigations. Support Risk Exposure Reporting, regulatory reviews, and updates to the Risk Management Program to meet evolving business and regulatory needs. Develop automations for robust supervision and risk management. Develop real-time monitoring systems to quickly identify adverse market conditions or operational issues. Implement a robust control testing framework to validate risk mitigation measures and the effectiveness of controls. Implement automated alert mechanisms for risk limit breaches, unusual trading patterns, and system anomalies. Leverage advanced analytics tools to uncover risk trends and provide actionable insights for decision-making. Build dashboards and reports using tools like Looker to visualize key risk metrics and inform stakeholders effectively. Telecommuting permitted.

What you bring

  • Bachelor’s degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science or related field plus five years of progressively responsible experience in job offered or related occupation.
  • Education and/or experience must include:
    • Apply Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and National Futures Association (NFA) regulatory requirements into risk controls, supervisory procedures, and program documentation;
    • Design and execute enterprise or Future Commission Merchant (FCM) level risk assessments;
    • Build and implement automations such as ETL data pipelines and scheduled data jobs (Airflow-type scheduling tools) to support risk monitoring;
    • Develop real-time or near–real-time monitoring and alerting systems that detect risk limit breaches, unusual trading activity, or system anomalies;
    • Execute control testing programs for risk mitigation;
    • Perform advanced statistical analytics on large structured datasets utilizing Python or similar programming tools to identify trends and quantify risk exposures;
    • Utilize industry-standard business intelligence or visualization platforms (Looker, Superset, Tableau, or PowerBI) to build dashboards, trend analyses, and key risk metric reporting; and
    • Investigate complex risk scenarios and develop mitigation strategies aligned with industry regulatory standards.
  • Background checks required

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
  • Best in class benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.
  • Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more.
  • Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
  • Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
  • Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to the corresponding compensation zone.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About the Opportunity

  • We are looking for an experienced Senior Manager, Settlement & Reconciliation to lead and enhance our settlement and reconciliation operations across both digital assets and fiat.
  • This role requires more than strong settlement operational experience. The ideal candidate should have a solid understanding of trading and settlement system architecture, including how settlement systems interact with trading platforms, transaction data, custody/banking infrastructure, and finance/accounting systems.
  • The role will serve as a key bridge between Finance, Settlement Operations, Product, Engineering, and other relevant stakeholders, translating settlement and accounting requirements into clear system, data, and reporting requirements.
  • Candidates with experience in traditional financial markets, securities, banking, brokerage, clearing, custody, or other transaction-intensive financial institutions are highly preferred.
 
  • The successful candidate will build a settlement and reconciliation function that is not only operationally effective, but also system-driven, highly reconcilable, and finance-ready.
  • The individual should be able to understand a transaction from execution through settlement, reconciliation, and ultimately financial accounting, and work across Operations, Finance, Product, Data, and Engineering to ensure that the underlying processes and systems are scalable, controlled, and transparent.
 

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Settlement Operations
    - Lead and oversee day-to-day settlement operations across digital asset and fiat transactions.
    - Ensure transactions are settled accurately, completely, and within the required timelines.
    - Establish and continuously improve settlement procedures, controls, exception handling, and escalation mechanisms.
    - Identify settlement breaks, operational risks, and process inefficiencies, and drive timely resolution.
    - Support new products, transaction flows, and business models by assessing their settlement and operational requirements.
  • Settlement System & System Architecture
    - Develop a strong understanding of the end-to-end settlement system architecture and transaction data flow.
    - Understand how settlement systems interface with:
      - Trading systems and order/transaction engines;
      - Wallet, custody, and blockchain infrastructure;
      - Fiat banking and payment systems;
      - Data warehouse and reporting platforms; and
      - Finance, accounting, and general ledger systems.
    - Work closely with Product and Engineering teams to define settlement-related system requirements.
    - Translate operational and finance requirements into clear and actionable data, system, and reporting specifications for Engineering teams.
    - Define the reports, data fields, transaction-level information, and reconciliation logic required to support settlement operations and financial accounting.
    - Participate in system implementation, enhancement, UAT, and post-implementation validation from a settlement and finance-control perspective.
  • Digital Asset Reconciliation
    - Own and oversee Digital Asset (DA) reconciliation, including reconciliation among customer balances, internal ledgers, wallet/on-chain balances, custody records, and other relevant source systems.
    - Investigate and resolve reconciliation differences, including transaction timing differences, system exceptions, missing transactions, and data inconsistencies.
    - Work with Product, Engineering, Data, Wallet, and Finance teams to identify root causes and implement sustainable remediation.
    - Establish appropriate reconciliation controls and monitoring mechanisms to ensure completeness and accuracy of digital asset balances and movements.
  • Fiat Reconciliation
    - Own and oversee Fiat reconciliation across customer balances, banking/custodian records, payment channels, internal operational systems, and the general ledger.
    - Ensure customer fiat assets and liabilities can be reconciled to relevant operational and accounting records.
    - Investigate reconciliation breaks and coordinate with Finance, Fiat Operations, Product, Engineering, banks, custodians, and payment service providers for resolution.
    - Drive automation and system improvements to reduce manual reconciliation and operational dependency.
  • Customer Transaction Reconciliation
    - Oversee transaction-level reconciliation covering customer trades, deposits, withdrawals, transfers, settlements, and other relevant transaction activities.
    - Ensure customer transaction records can be traced consistently across trading, settlement, operational, and accounting systems.
    - Establish effective exception-management processes for unmatched or incomplete transactions.
    - Support Finance and external audit requirements by ensuring transaction data and reconciliation evidence are complete, accurate, and traceable.
  •  Finance & Accounting Support
    - Partner closely with Finance to ensure settlement data and reports provide sufficient information for accurate and timely accounting.
    - Understand how trading and settlement activities ultimately flow into financial records and the general ledger.
    - Define operational reports and data outputs required by Finance for:
      - Accounting entries;
      - Period-end closing;
      - Balance sheet reconciliation;
      - Customer asset and liability reconciliation; and
      - Financial and external audit support.
    - Identify gaps between operational systems and accounting requirements and work with relevant teams to develop scalable solutions.
  • Process, Control & Team Management
    - Build and maintain robust settlement and reconciliation SOPs, controls, and governance frameworks.
    - Drive automation and process improvements to improve settlement efficiency, accuracy, scalability, and control.
    - Establish key operational metrics and monitor settlement exceptions, reconciliation breaks, aging items, and resolution timelines.
    - Manage and develop the settlement team, ensuring clear ownership, effective prioritization, and strong execution.
    - Act as a senior escalation point for complex settlement, reconciliation, and transaction-related issues.
    - Collaborate effectively with cross-functional stakeholders across Finance, Product, Engineering, Data, Operations, Risk, Compliance, and other relevant teams.
 

What We Look For In You

  • Bachelor’s degree or above in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
  • Significant experience in settlement, clearing, reconciliation, transaction operations, custody, or related financial operations, with experience in a managerial or senior leadership role.
  • Strong experience with customer transaction reconciliation and transaction-level data analysis.
  • Solid understanding of trading lifecycle and settlement processes.
  • Prior experience in traditional financial institutions, such as banks, securities firms, broker-dealers, exchanges, clearing houses, custodians, payment institutions, or other transaction-intensive financial businesses.

Who We Are

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.
 

About The Opportunity

Our mission is to drive user growth and engagement across global markets by building a scalable growth platform — the shared campaign engine, task and incentive systems, loyalty programs, and ToB operational tooling that power growth for every business line at OKX — and by unlocking acquisition through diversified channels including SEO, ASO, affiliate, referral, and paid.
As the Growth Platform Product Lead, you will own the product vision and roadmap for our growth middle-platform, lead a team of product managers, and act as the central partner to business, channel, and regional stakeholders who rely on the platform to hit their growth targets. This is a leadership role for someone who has built growth infrastructure at scale and knows how to turn a fragmented set of campaign tools into a unified, self-serve growth system.

What You’ll Be Doing 

Own the Growth Platform Strategy
  • Define the multi-year vision and roadmap for the growth middle-platform: campaign engine, task/mission system, rewards and incentive infrastructure, loyalty and tiering, user segmentation and targeting, and the ToB configuration and analytics layer that operators use daily.
  • Set platform standards for reusability, configurability, and time-to-launch so that new growth activities can be shipped by business teams without bespoke engineering.
  • Balance platform investment against business-line requests, and make clear, well-communicated prioritization calls.
Build the Platform
  • Lead the design and delivery of ToC growth products (campaigns, tasks, mega sales, loyalty) and the ToB capabilities behind them (campaign configuration, rules engine, budget and risk controls, reporting).
  • Drive experimentation infrastructure and growth analytics so that every campaign is measurable, comparable, and optimizable.
  • Leverage AI tools and automation to shorten experimentation cycles, surface insights faster, and scale growth operations with fewer manual touchpoints.
Enable Channel Growth
  • Partner with channel owners across SEO, ASO, referral, affiliate, and paid to translate channel-specific funnel needs into platform capabilities.
  • Identify high-leverage channel opportunities and build the platform features that amplify channel performance across markets.
Manage Stakeholders Across the Organization
  • Serve as the single point of accountability for the growth platform with Trading, Listing, Paid Ads, Content, Affiliate, Referral, regional growth teams, and risk/compliance.
  • Establish intake, prioritization, and governance processes that keep dozens of concurrent stakeholders aligned and informed.
  • Influence senior leadership on platform investment, trade-offs, and sequencing; resolve conflicts between business urgency and platform integrity.
Lead and Grow the Team
  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of product managers; set clear goals, review work quality, and build a high-performance culture.
  • Raise the bar on PM craft across the team: problem framing, data literacy, spec quality, and cross-functional execution.

What We Look For In You 

  • 5+ years of product management experience, including 2+ years managing product managers and owning a multi-quarter roadmap.
  • Deep growth middle-platform experience: you have designed and shipped a campaign engine, task/mission system, incentive or rewards platform, loyalty program, or comparable shared growth infrastructure that served multiple business lines.

  • Exceptional stakeholder management: demonstrated ability to run intake and prioritization across many competing internal customers, manage up to executive leadership, and hold the line on platform trade-offs without losing partner trust.

  • High learning velocity: able to rapidly internalize new domains — crypto, regional markets, new channels — and connect product, data, and market signals into actionable strategy.

  • Experience in crypto, fintech, or other regulated consumer products where growth mechanics must satisfy risk and compliance constraints.
  • Hands-on experience with SEO and/or ASO strategy, including keyword optimization, app store listing optimization, and organic growth levers.
